chunks: Zurārah and Muḥammad ibn Muslim narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:
"Any man who has wealth, and a year passes over it, then he pays zakat on it."
It was said to him: "Then if he gifts it away a month before its year, or by a day?" He said: "Then nothing is upon him."
And Zurārah narrated from him that he said:

"This is only like a man who breaks his fast one day in the month of Ramaḍān while resident, then goes out at the end of the day on a journey, intending by that journey to invalidate the kaffārah that had become obligatory upon him."

key_terms.الْحَوْلُ: The completion of a lunar year over wealth.
key_terms.الْكَفَّارَةِ: The expiation that became obligatory due to breaking the fast.
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: The month of Ramaḍān, in which fasting is obligatory.
key_terms.شَيْءٌ: Anything obligatory or due in this context.
key_terms.مَالٌ: Wealth or property subject to zakat consideration.
key_terms.وَهَبَهُ: He gave it away as a gift.

ai.seo_question: Is zakat still obligatory if someone gives away their wealth just before the zakat year is completed?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on zakat: when wealth remains in a person's possession for a full year, zakat becomes due on it. If the wealth is gifted away before the year is completed, then zakat is not due. The Imam عليه السلام then compares this to someone trying to use travel after deliberately breaking a Ramaḍān fast in order to evade the kaffārah already incurred.
